title: The Federal Reserve just pumped about $31 billion ...
content:
The Federal Reserve just pumped about $31 billion into the banking system through overnight repo operations which sounds alarming until you understand what's actually happening. 
Yes, it's the largest liquidity injection since COVID but that's almost entirely because of year end window dressing.
This is a completely predictable and routine seasonal event that has nothing to do with systemic stress in the financial system.
At  year end, banks deliberately shrink their balance sheets temporarily because regulators measure bank health using capital ratios calculated on the last day of the quarter.
If a bank shrinks its balance sheet on December 31st, those regulatory metrics look pristine on paper, even if the bank's actual financial position hasn't changed at all. 
Academic research shows banks routinely reduce repo borrowing by 12 to 25 percent around quarter ends, and that's exactly what happened in now.
When banks collectively pull back from the repo market to clean up their balance sheets for regulatory reporting, it creates a temporary cash shortage that's purely mechanical and seasonal. 
There's nothing to worry about here, this is just the plumbing of finance working exactly as designed.

title: The US Dollar just had its worst year in nearly a ...
content:
The US Dollar just had its worst year in nearly a decade, dropping about 9% in value against other major currencies like the Euro and Yen. 
This is a massive U turn from 2024, when the dollar was super strong  and it signals that the global financial tides have shifted dramatically. 
When you see a drop this big, it usually means big investors are moving their money out of the US and into other countries because they aren't getting paid as much interest to hold dollars anymore. 
In 2025, the Federal Reserve (the US central bank)  cut interest rates to try and help the economy or save jobs, and when rates go down, the incentive to hold dollars goes down with them.
For you personally, this has a few direct impacts.
 First, if you’re planning a trip to Europe or Japan, your vacation just got significantly more expensive because your dollars don't swap for as many Euros or Yen as they did a year ago. 
Second, anything we import from other countries like cars, electronics, or fancy cheese costs more to bring in, which can keep inflation sticking around longer than we’d like. 
However, it’s not all bad news. 
A weak dollar is actually like rocket fuel for asset prices; when the dollar goes down, things priced in dollars like the S&P 500, Silver and Gold often go up because it takes more "weaker" dollars to buy them.
It also helps US companies sell more products abroad because their goods become cheaper for foreigners to buy.
As for where we are headed, the smart money (hedge funds) is betting that this drop isn't over yet. 
These funds have turned bearish meaning they expect the dollar to keep falling. 
This creates a trend where the dollar could continue to slide into 2026, especially if the Federal Reserve keeps cutting interest rates to save the economy and the job market. 
If the Fed continues its easy money policies, we will likely see the dollar weaken further, which would be great for your investment portfolio but painful for your grocery bill and travel plans. 
We are essentially in a cycle where the government is prioritizing keeping the stock market and economy afloat over keeping the currency strong.
The US Dollar experienced a historic decline in 2025:
The US Dollar Index fell -9% in 2025, marking its worst performance since 2017.
This represents a sharp reversal from the +8% gain recorded in 2024.
Excluding 2017, this was the weakest year for the currency since 2003.
Since 2010, there have been only 5 years in which the US Dollar posted an annual decline.
Meanwhile, hedge fund positioning on the US Dollar turned bearish as of the week ending December 16th, the first time since mid-October, according to CFTC data.
Fed policy will drive the next move in the US Dollar. 
- 
The Kobeissi Letter

: Skill + Nano Banana + GitHub Action + Vercel Deploy: Blog Automation
I’ve been trying to build this automation for a long time, but the results were always pretty bad.
Link: 
https://t.co/e784FO6XPd
Until several technology advances finally came together. Here’s the full process of how I’m doing it today... and how I plan to keep improving it:
1- Claude Skills:
A Skill that searches for the component I want to write about. I review the component, go through Anthropic’s documentation for that component, and get the perfect context to write the blog post.
The Skill comes with a solid blog structure, a Mermaid diagram, installation instructions, usage, and results. 100% validated by me. This is how I use Agents, Commands, Settings, Hooks, MCPs, and Skills.
2- Nano Banana:
I create the blog cover with Nano Banana. I don’t need a fancy cover with tons of colors and design. Tech blogs are direct and to the point. Devs don’t really care about heavy design.
3- GitHub Action:
I run this process once a day to create a blog post about one of the most downloaded components on 
https://t.co/pEjytZiAFd
. It’s great that the community keeps sharing components, but if we don’t know how and when to use them, the most important part is lost.
4- Vercel Deploy:
Automatic deploy with the new blog ready and published.
Future improvements:
- Add a pre-deploy step to review the blog before publishing. Right now, I review directly in production and send a hotfix if I find improvements.
- Telegram notification with a blog preview, so I can read it, request changes directly from Claude via Telegram, and then approve the deploy.
- Discord notification so the community knows a new blog has been published.
- Trigger this process every time I approve a PR for a new component contributed by the community to the repo.
Fully open source:

title: Since November 2019, essential goods and services ...
content:
Since November 2019, essential goods and services that most Americans rely on every day have become dramatically more expensive. 
The increases are far larger than the official inflation numbers most people hear about. 
Motor vehicle insurance has been the worst offender, jumping 56.1%. 
That means if you were paying $100 a month for car insurance in late 2019, you're now paying roughly $156 per month for the same coverage. 
Utility bills have climbed 48.8%, car maintenance another 48.8%, coffee prices 46.1%, and electricity 40.4%. 
Even meat and eating out have jumped 38.1% and 34.8% respectively. 
All of these categories have dramatically outpaced the headline inflation rate of 26%, which is the number you typically see in news headlines.
Here's what matters, basic necessities, the things you absolutely cannot avoid buying have inflated far faster than the aggregate number suggests. 
You can't opt out of car insurance if you own a vehicle. 
You can't choose not to use electricity or heat your home.
This means real purchasing power has deteriorated far more for ordinary households than the 26% headline inflation indicates.
Prices of basic necessities have seen a historic surge in the US:
Since November 2019, motor vehicle insurance costs have soared +56.1%, the largest increase of any major consumer category.
Utility gas service and motor vehicle maintenance costs have both surged +48.8%, followed by a +46.1% increase in coffee prices.
Electricity prices alone have jumped +40.4% over the same period.
Meanwhile, meats, poultry, and fish prices have climbed +38.1%, while food away from home has risen +34.8%.
All of these categories have far outpaced the +26% increase in headline CPI inflation.
Only asset owners are protected from compounding inflation. 
- 
The Kobeissi Letter

title: "MAN'S LIFE COMES IN SEASONS"
content:
"MAN'S LIFE COMES IN SEASONS"
if you don't have a visceral level of disgust at who you used to be, you haven't grown. calibrating this perfectly is the tricky part 
contempt bordering on shame at the way you used to do things...a healthy self-loathing...without veering into depressive spirals or negative/self-destructive feedback loops.
this applies universally i.e. if reading shit you wrote 5 years ago doesn’t make you cringe, you haven’t improved as a writer.
if you look back at yourself 5 years ago and say - "yup, I had it figured out then, and I've got it figured out now" - oh boy...you gon' learn brother lol. 
think they say "there's only two types of leaders, those who have been humbled and those who are about to be."
(2/4)
its like when you're catching up with someone
"hows so-and-so doing"
"oh you know, hes the exact same." 
I suppose this is a Rorschach test, but if you're the same at 40 as you were at 35, 30, and 25...that's alarming & arguably tragic
Munger's "any year that you don't destroy one of your best-loved ideas is a wasted year"...and this mf just strung 15 back-to-back
I said 5 yrs, Munger says one - hes usually right. 
So really, your worldview should be changing constantly...rapid one-year lookbacks.
high bar to us...but to a great mind like his? 
as philosopher-king randy moss once said: "what's ten grand, to me...aint shit. next time I might shake my d***."
--
(3/4)
imo this more than anything else (changes in your worldview/in the way you think) are what people are picking up on when they say "you changed." 
subtle yet totally-altered perception...generally have found the correct paths all --> melancholic and austere.
but ppl have a natural antipathy to the word "change." comes from defining it wrong. 
to me "change" and "grow" are synonyms. 
who the f changes for the worse? intentionally, I mean. I suppose it does happen to people. But in general you should want to change, and free-associate positive change = progress.
(4/4)
what is actionable about this...
I have found there are two things that change you: books and experience. 
there may be more than two. those two are the ones I can 100% guarantee each time...bulletproof...with experience of course meaning "pain," failure, fucking up.
that's the acid test, for the 1-year lookbacks...
"have you changed?"
if not...you're not reading, you're not getting out of your comfort zone, or both. 
thats the alarm, the warning, the impetus to go shake shit up. 
God put you here for a reason...don't let the man down.

title: risk articles (cont).
content:
risk articles (cont). 
all these risk articles hinge on what I feel like should just be an absolute. its the same balance or tension phrased many different ways
1. stops vs fundamentals. 
if you're fundamentally-driven, a stop-loss runs counter to the entire philosophy (i.e. a stock goes from 10x to 9x and you stop out)
2. risk mgr hat vs fundamental hat
similar issue...stop-out is -15%, stock gets -10% but fundamentally you think this is a mkt mispricing/inefficiency, and would love to own it -20%
now you're effectively operating without process, where you use stops, except for when you pull your stops as you see fit.
which hat are you wearing? risk hat or fundamental hat? or do you pick and choose based on the weather?
this is why I say, needs to be orchestrated high-level...
3. is red P&L opportunity or risk
simpler to visualize, but have gotten replies saying...some positions opportunity, some positions are risk.
mentally I'm not sure that's going to be a consistent, sustainable + repeatable risk mgmt framework?
how do you determine which is which, does it ever change, can you quantify this somehow? or is "discretionary" the answer? 
too much discretion there imo. too soft, too loose, too flexible and hand-wavy...works in a calm tape...in a fast tape you'll get crossed up and find yourself operating "discretionary" as a synonym for zero sell discipline --> immediate DD% drawdown w/ process in shambles
--
HERO WORSHIP CIRCULAR REFERENCE ERROR:
wrote this up about an earlier period in my life (~10-15 yrs ago, jr analyst) to illustrate the balance...same tension, different expression of it
"...Meanwhile, about a decade ago I was at war with myself, a mind full of discord and agita, hopelessly trying to answer the question:
“What do I actually believe?”
After watching a great PM and risk manager in action, my takeaway was fairly simple.
“I should start trading with stops.”
So I’d put them in, sometimes… because other Smart Guys said you should learn to take pain and absorb volatility. I was reading a lot of Buffett and Munger at the time. The market transfers money from the impatient to the patient, wrote Buffett himself. He also said to be greedy when others are fearful, to make Mr. Market your slave and not your master, and so that means you gotta be willing to buy more when you’re down.
“How do I put in a stop-loss without going against Buffett?”
Shit.
Maybe I shouldn’t trade with stops. Plus, I’m a fundamental analyst, so yes, the P&L may be red, but what kind of fundamental analyst would let that get in the way of his views? Where in my Excel model does the P&L determine my probability-weighted price target, 50-50% derived P/E and EV/EBITDA, with a toggle for a third table incorporating FCF Yield % just for extra precision [read: mental masturbation]? 
But I couldn’t reconcile two opposing views, one, that risk is to be managed and losses are to be cut, but two, why I should sell a position in a high-quality business where the risk/reward is only improving in my favor?
This was the first time, but not the last, that I was stuck in a Hero Worship circular reference error. For many years, way longer than I should have, I wanted to be all the great investors and traders at the exact same time. Instead, I was able to find perfect mediocrity in the middle, doing nothing right by not wanting to box myself into one style.
In this case, I split the difference…if it’s a trade, I’ll add stops. If it’s a fundamental investment, no stops. The criteria for determining which is which, was “I’ll figure it out.”
Those were the rules for a while. Call it 50-50 stops versus no stops. There’s “north star” (stop-biased) and there’s “hard and fast,” (100% stops) and I went with “north star.”

title: more risk snippets from the cutting room floor
content:
more risk snippets from the cutting room floor
--
After that, year by year, I would see “smart fundamental guys” get carried out, over and over and over.
“Stocks can trade at any price” – a legendary quote, instantly enshrined in Canton, and one that I recall being in tandem with a Baby Buffett cover.
Over time, it also became clear that “something unprecedented just happened” doesn’t really hold water as an outlier. Every single day in markets, something unprecedented happens.
It also became abundantly clear that with rare exceptions, the market is always right. You rarely know why you’re down 10% or 20%...and the market will eventually fill you in on what you’re missing, but only once you’re down 50%.
In Smart Fundamental Guy language, "I sell when my thesis breaks" - the mkt told you it was broken down 20%...the "confirmation" only arrives down 50%.
--
At the juncture of “smart fundamental guy” versus “risk manager,” the SAME call has taken every single investor out of the game ever:
“the market is wrong and I am right.”
As soon as you say that, you have signed your own death warrant.
--
Mistake two, when you officially declare war on the market – ie you say “I’m a fundamental analyst now, and not a risk manager” - your entire process completely inverts.
Before, “red P&L means I’m wrong.”
After, “red P&L means fundamentally cheaper, so I’m even more right.”
You might have positions with stops, but mentally, you’re no longer trading from that frame of mind...you have no stops, no protection...you’re exposed.
Risk no longer exists, and the veil of Maya has been pulled over your eyes.
What you previously saw as risk, now you only see volatility.
The soothing relief of bagholder quotes...
“Volatility is the friend of the long-term investor”...
Risk is only permanent capital impairment…
This is just Mr. Market being manic and offering you discounts…
The margin of safety has only increased, a voting machine and not a weighing machine, transferring money from the impatient to the patient.
--
For all the good I can say about Buffett, I also believe that blindly following his advice, from a risk management perspective, has caused financial ruin for many people.
Using the Smart Fundamental Guy framework, there is no such thing as risk management.
Why?
Because there is no risk to manage.
Remember, volatility is not risk...the only risk is permanent capital impairment.
I will get ahead of the obvious question.
Q: “How do you know if it’s a permanent capital impairment or not?”
A: You don’t.
Stocks all look the same when they're down 50%. The market doesn't give a little wink-wink, nudge-nudge. "pssst...I'm impermanent fyi."
Even Buffett will tell you it's not easy to tell the difference. An individual investor has no chance.
This arrogant logic has probably led to more “game over” screens than anything else, even more than 0DTE options, because while the option autist knows he’s a degenerate gambler, the smart fundamental Buffett zombie genuinely believes that he’s smarter than the market…
there is no possible scenario where he’s wrong…it never once crosses his mind, and he will fight the market all the way to zero.
Everything Buffett says should be applied to the S&P 500 and nothing else (by an individual).
--
...That gets us to my approach today, which may be right or may be wrong depending on which Smart Guy you worship.
The first principles of this risk management philosophy, to put it gently, are “I don’t give a fuck”…meaning, for every single position, there is a price at which I know I’m getting out.
When that price arrives, I don't give a fuck about the market or about anything fundamental - I am OUT.
When P&L and fundamentals conflict, 100% of the time the P&L wins out, end of story...I simply don’t care.
The mindset at all times is:
1. Protect the P&L
2. Don’t draw down
3. Preserve mental capital
That is it.
Everything else is basicall[...]

title: super grateful for all the good people on here, we...
content:
super grateful for all the good people on here, weird little shit
the basic kindness/appreciation/courtesy in a world seemingly devoid of it…roses grown in concrete
ppl who came exploding out of nowhere w/ a 4 page rock bottom DM…felt the catharsis…can relate, happy to help 
ppl who reply with respectful and thoughtful angles that helped me think differently 
young cats who have that fire…the HUNGER to win…shit fills my heart with light 
ppl who only like my “pain” tweets and nothing more…I know ur waging war in silence…idk what…but u just gotta KEEP SHOWING UP TO LIFE - PERIOD. 
ppl who reply w just “I needed that” - my favorite imho - means something in there lit a spark + made a difference…all this shit is about 
all humans are the same - behind the masks, everyone wants the same things. never treat anyone better or worse than you….all equals, God’s creations…
fight like a mf to keep that love for your fellow man in your heart, no matter what. ppl will try and dim that shit…do not let them… it’s very hard to lose w/ a heart full of love, everything just seems to gravitate into ur orbit
energy is contagious - never forget that…whatever room ur in, whatever mood, one person can swing the entire vibe
God bless…ignore the crowd, bring what u uniquely bring to the table…and have faith that whatever energy you put out, is what the universe will bring back to you. it has never been any other way
“IF THERE IS LIGHT IN YOUR HEART, YOU WILL FIND YOUR WAY HOME.”
